LESSON: JEWELLERY AND ORNAMENTATION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: FINE ARTS FOR LEARNERS WITH LOW VISION JUNE
Strand: Indigenous Crafts (3D Art)
Topic 3.4: Jewellery and Ornamentation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Jewellery and Ornamentation, part of Indigenous Crafts (3D Art) in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 FINE ARTS FOR LEARNERS WITH LOW VISION JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does jewellery and ornamentation contribute to environmental conservation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Jewellery and Ornamentation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The skill of making observation is acquired as the learner explores the

environment, collects and prepares materials for leatherwork and jewellery while producing various functional and

decorative items.

• Communication: The skill of team work is nurtured as the learner;

- seeks information and offers support while sourcing, preparing, using materials and sharing what they have learnt

with others.

The skill of listening is acquired as the learner;

- Pays attention to the person speaking, takes turns in conversation during critique of own and others’ Mixed Media

artworks.

• Collaboration: The skill of teamwork is acquired as the learner amicably works together with peers, appreciates efforts

of others while sourcing materials for leatherwork and jewellery.

Values:
Respect: Learner appreciates diverse opinions and values human dignity during critique sessions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Health promotion issues: Learner is sensitized on the need to consider hygiene when collecting and cleaning found

objects

• Social economic and environmental issues: Learner observes safety measures when using sharp tools used in

leatherwork and jewellery.
